blocks.text: Dohra:
S. Baaj Singh ransacked most of the territory, With the support of all the Khalsa forces. All the Muslim towns which came to his notice, Were occupied even if these were remotely situated. (1)
lines: S.
Baaj Singh ransacked most of the territory,
With the support of all the Khalsa forces.
All the Muslim towns which came to his notice,
Were occupied even if these were remotely situated.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Whenever S. Baaj Singh happened to mount his steed, He would stamp over a Muslim's head (to use it as a step ladder). When this news of S. Baaj Singh's crushing a Muslim's head (daily) spread around, All the Muslims ran to far off places from Sirhind. (2)
lines: Whenever S.
Baaj Singh happened to mount his steed,
He would stamp over a Muslim's head (to use it as a step ladder).
When this news of S.
Baaj Singh's crushing a Muslim's head (daily) spread around,
All the Muslims ran to far off places from Sirhind.

blocks.text: Whosoever came into confrontation was conquered (by the Singhs), Such was the defeat that fell to the Mughal forces' share. One of the sons of Wazir Khan who had survived the occupation of (the Sirhind), Was able to muster the support of many residents of Punjab. (3)
lines: Whosoever came into confrontation was conquered (by the Singhs),
Such was the defeat that fell to the Mughal forces' share.
One of the sons of Wazir Khan who had survived the occupation of (the Sirhind),
Was able to muster the support of many residents of Punjab.

blocks.text: They went and appealed to the (Mughal emperor) Bahadur Shah, Who was camping in the South (at that time). They complained that (Banda Singh) had ransacked all the Mughal territories, As well as abolished Prophet Mohammad's religion of Islam. (4)
lines: They went and appealed to the (Mughal emperor) Bahadur Shah,
Who was camping in the South (at that time).
They complained that (Banda Singh) had ransacked all the Mughal territories,
As well as abolished Prophet Mohammad's religion of Islam.

blocks.text: Dohra:

They warned that (Banda Singh) would capture both Delhi and Lahore as well, If the Mughal emperor did not intervene (and send his force there). The people of Punjab had already turned against the Mughal rule, Together with the people of foot hills and hill states of upper regions. (5)
lines: They warned that (Banda Singh) would capture both Delhi and Lahore as well,
If the Mughal emperor did not intervene (and send his force there).
The people of Punjab had already turned against the Mughal rule,
Together with the people of foot hills and hill states of upper regions.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Banda Singh's writ was running large (all over the region), As he had created anarchic conditions of the worst kind. He has created havoc and chaos all over the country, And spread his fame through his acts of arson and chastisement. (6)
lines: Banda Singh's writ was running large (all over the region),
As he had created anarchic conditions of the worst kind.
He has created havoc and chaos all over the country,
And spread his fame through his acts of arson and chastisement.

blocks.text: When the Emperor asked about Banda Singh's identity, The people replied that he was a camp follower of Guru Gobind Singh. The Guru had sent him to avenge the death of his sons, And Banda had killed Wazir Khan (the Nawab of Sirhind) in an instant. (7)
lines: When the Emperor asked about Banda Singh's identity,
The people replied that he was a camp follower of Guru Gobind Singh.
The Guru had sent him to avenge the death of his sons,
And Banda had killed Wazir Khan (the Nawab of Sirhind) in an instant.

blocks.text: He had also killed all the four Malerkotla1 Pathan brothers, Who had seized a part of the Guru's treasure (from the battle of Anandpur). Since one of these Pathan brothers had protested against Sahibzadas execution, The Khalsa forces had spared the town of Malerkotla from being torched. (8)
lines: He had also killed all the four Malerkotla1 Pathan brothers,
Who had seized a part of the Guru's treasure (from the battle of Anandpur).
Since one of these Pathan brothers had protested against Sahibzadas execution,
The Khalsa forces had spared the town of Malerkotla from being torched.

blocks.text: They had captured the town of Samana and killed its custodian, Along with all the twenty two other custodians of that area. They had ransacked Sadhaura and burnt the (dead body) of its Pir, Whose shadow on a Hindu's dead body would make it immune from fire. (9)
lines: They had captured the town of Samana and killed its custodian,
Along with all the twenty two other custodians of that area.
They had ransacked Sadhaura and burnt the (dead body) of its Pir,
Whose shadow on a Hindu's dead body would make it immune from fire.

blocks.text: (Banda Singh) had cast a spell on the sharp weapons to render these ineffective, As well as he had the power to fly to any place wherever he wished. No canon, arrow or sword could ever hit his physical body, As he could repulse their attack with the sign of a finger. (10)
lines: (Banda Singh) had cast a spell on the sharp weapons to render these ineffective,
As well as he had the power to fly to any place wherever he wished.
No canon, arrow or sword could ever hit his physical body,
As he could repulse their attack with the sign of a finger.

blocks.text: Dohra:

His feet did not touch the ground as he walked on earth, Nor did his eyelids bat (when he opened his eyes). His shadow did not fall on earth (as he stood or sat), Such were the stories people had narrated about him. (11)
lines: His feet did not touch the ground as he walked on earth,
Nor did his eyelids bat (when he opened his eyes).
His shadow did not fall on earth (as he stood or sat),
Such were the stories people had narrated about him.

blocks.text: Sortha:

After hearing (all these tales about Banda Singh), Bahadur Shah felt extremely terrified in his heart of hearts. He refused to listen to any of people's complaints and Remarked that Banda Singh had been blessed with power by the Guru. (12)
lines: After hearing (all these tales about Banda Singh),
Bahadur Shah felt extremely terrified in his heart of hearts.
He refused to listen to any of people's complaints and Remarked that Banda Singh had been blessed with power by the Guru.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

As the emperor had a thorough knowledge about Guru Gobind Singh's powers, He did not pay any attention to the people's appeals. After hearing so much about Banda Singh's power of performing miracles, Bahadur Shah shook his head (as a mark of his helplessness). (13)
lines: As the emperor had a thorough knowledge about Guru Gobind Singh's powers,
He did not pay any attention to the people's appeals.
After hearing so much about Banda Singh's power of performing miracles,
Bahadur Shah shook his head (as a mark of his helplessness).

blocks.text: If the emperor Bahadur Shah waged a war against Banda Singh, He might get the emperor killed through some miracle or magic spell. In that case he would be committing an act of betrayal against the Guru, As well as stand deprived of his own sovereign rule. (14)
lines: If the emperor Bahadur Shah waged a war against Banda Singh,
He might get the emperor killed through some miracle or magic spell.
In that case he would be committing an act of betrayal against the Guru,
As well as stand deprived of his own sovereign rule.

blocks.text: Considering both the options (of waging a war or betraying the Guru) as equally risky, He was fascinated by the lure of political power as well. Banda Singh was sure to kill him in an open confrontation, As he possessed great power of performing miracles. (15)
lines: Considering both the options (of waging a war or betraying the Guru) as equally risky,
He was fascinated by the lure of political power as well.
Banda Singh was sure to kill him in an open confrontation,
As he possessed great power of performing miracles.

blocks.text: Banda Singh could get him eliminated at any movement, As he could summon the services of spirits (to carryout his command). That was why he did not accede to the people's plea, Nor did he bother about (the loss of power) around Lahore. (16)
lines: Banda Singh could get him eliminated at any movement,
As he could summon the services of spirits (to carryout his command).
That was why he did not accede to the people's plea,
Nor did he bother about (the loss of power) around Lahore.

blocks.text: Dohra:

They had heard that Banda Singh had planted the flag posts, And hoisted (the Khalsa's saffron flags) up to town of Panipat. And that if ever the Mughal forces crossed Past these flags, They would get automatically destroyed (there and then). (17)
lines: They had heard that Banda Singh had planted the flag posts,
And hoisted (the Khalsa's saffron flags) up to town of Panipat.
And that if ever the Mughal forces crossed Past these flags,
They would get automatically destroyed (there and then).

blocks.text: Chaupai:

(The Emperor Bahadur Shah) felt scared after hearing these accounts, Which made him desist from advancing towards Punjab. Even as petitioners from Punjab kept on pleading before him, Nobody else came forward to render any assistance. (18)
lines: (The Emperor Bahadur Shah) felt scared after hearing these accounts,
Which made him desist from advancing towards Punjab.
Even as petitioners from Punjab kept on pleading before him,
Nobody else came forward to render any assistance.

blocks.text: No (army commander) wished to discuss this issue with the king, Lest he should be asked to lead a campaign (against Banda Singh). As Banda Singh was held in as much awe as that of a lion (in a forest), The Muslims kept confined to their homes in awe of Banda Singh. (19)
lines: No (army commander) wished to discuss this issue with the king,
Lest he should be asked to lead a campaign (against Banda Singh).
As Banda Singh was held in as much awe as that of a lion (in a forest),
The Muslims kept confined to their homes in awe of Banda Singh.

blocks.text: The (prime) minister did not broach this topic with the emperor, Lest he himself might be deputed to hold negotiations (with Banda Singh). No existing custodian volunteered to take over the command of (Punjab), As they pretended complete ignorance about the whole affair. (20)
lines: The (prime) minister did not broach this topic with the emperor,
Lest he himself might be deputed to hold negotiations (with Banda Singh).
No existing custodian volunteered to take over the command of (Punjab),
As they pretended complete ignorance about the whole affair.

blocks.text: They did not hold even their own courts regularly, Lest the emperor should depute them to proceed (to Punjab). Feeling sure that Banda Singh, being omniscient about every thing, Might get them eliminated even if they thought of talking ill of him. (21)
lines: They did not hold even their own courts regularly,
Lest the emperor should depute them to proceed (to Punjab).
Feeling sure that Banda Singh, being omniscient about every thing,
Might get them eliminated even if they thought of talking ill of him.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Then the Punjabi (Muslims) protested wearing (black) robes, And took out torch-light processions against the emperor, But the emperor did not pay any attention to their protests, And kept on lying low and brooding silently over the problems. (22)
lines: Then the Punjabi (Muslims) protested wearing (black) robes,
And took out torch-light processions against the emperor,
But the emperor did not pay any attention to their protests,
And kept on lying low and brooding silently over the problems.

blocks.text: Then all the members of the Muslim clergy and religious mendicants, Together with the Hajees2 and Pirs (joined this protest). They accused the emperor of turning a kafir3 and a heretic, Raising the pitch of their protest to such a great extent. (23)
lines: Then all the members of the Muslim clergy and religious mendicants,
Together with the Hajees2 and Pirs (joined this protest).
They accused the emperor of turning a kafir3 and a heretic,
Raising the pitch of their protest to such a great extent.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Some of them accused the emperor of giving up his religion, And no longer belonging to the Islamic ideological order (of prophet Mohammed4 ). They sermonised that the prophet would not vouch for him (on the day of judgement), And he would be cast into hell (to rot there forever). (24)
lines: Some of them accused the emperor of giving up his religion,
And no longer belonging to the Islamic ideological order (of prophet Mohammed4 ).
They sermonised that the prophet would not vouch for him (on the day of judgement),
And he would be cast into hell (to rot there forever).

blocks.text: They charged him of having sold himself to the Hindus, As if they had conferred the sovereignty on him (instead of his own ancestors). They reminded him that Prophet Mohammed had conferred the sovereignty on Mughals, And he had got that sovereignty in a hierarchical inheritance. (25)
lines: They charged him of having sold himself to the Hindus,
As if they had conferred the sovereignty on him (instead of his own ancestors).
They reminded him that Prophet Mohammed had conferred the sovereignty on Mughals,
And he had got that sovereignty in a hierarchical inheritance.

blocks.text: They accused him of lowering the prestige of Muslim Pirs, Who were capable of showering all kinds of blessings on him. They blamed him for crediting the Hindus for his sovereignty, As if the Muslim Pirs were incapable of conferring this boon. (26)
lines: They accused him of lowering the prestige of Muslim Pirs,
Who were capable of showering all kinds of blessings on him.
They blamed him for crediting the Hindus for his sovereignty,
As if the Muslim Pirs were incapable of conferring this boon.

blocks.text: They threatened to block his passage by brandishing naked daggers, And even stabbing him directly in the chest. They warned that the whole Muslim world up to Mecca would condemn his (inaction), And the Prophet Mohammed would not vouch for him (on the judgement day). (27)
lines: They threatened to block his passage by brandishing naked daggers,
And even stabbing him directly in the chest.
They warned that the whole Muslim world up to Mecca would condemn his (inaction),
And the Prophet Mohammed would not vouch for him (on the judgement day).

blocks.text: Someone claimed that he had just returned from Mecca (after performing Haj), Where he had heard people talking about (Bahadur Shah's lapse of duty). He had heard that Bahadur Shah had been enamoured by the Hindus, And he had bartered away his religion for the sake of power. (28)
lines: Someone claimed that he had just returned from Mecca (after performing Haj),
Where he had heard people talking about (Bahadur Shah's lapse of duty).
He had heard that Bahadur Shah had been enamoured by the Hindus,
And he had bartered away his religion for the sake of power.

blocks.text: By declaring that he had been conferred with sovereignty by the Hindus, He had lowered the prestige of Prophet Mohammed. They influenced the emperor through such admonitions and rebuffs, And persuaded him repeatedly (to act against Banda Singh). (29)
lines: By declaring that he had been conferred with sovereignty by the Hindus,
He had lowered the prestige of Prophet Mohammed.
They influenced the emperor through such admonitions and rebuffs,
And persuaded him repeatedly (to act against Banda Singh).

blocks.text: The Episode of Travari5
Dohra:

(The Muslim clergymen) held out such threats (to Bahadur Shah), And passed several sarcastic strictures against him. The Muslim Pirs and Hajees joined together (in a conspiracy), And swore to (incite the emperor) by placing their hands on the holy Koran. (30)
lines: (The Muslim clergymen) held out such threats (to Bahadur Shah),
And passed several sarcastic strictures against him.
The Muslim Pirs and Hajees joined together (in a conspiracy),
And swore to (incite the emperor) by placing their hands on the holy Koran.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

The Muslim Pirs gave a solemn assurance (to the Emperor), That they would lead the expedition (against Banda Singh) after reciting the holy commandments. They would walk in front while carrying the holy Koran in their hands, And the Emperor should follow them with his Mughal army. (31)
lines: The Muslim Pirs gave a solemn assurance (to the Emperor),
That they would lead the expedition (against Banda Singh) after reciting the holy commandments.
They would walk in front while carrying the holy Koran in their hands,
And the Emperor should follow them with his Mughal army.

blocks.text: (After so many assurances), the emperor acceded to their request, But he promised to proceed up to the city of Agra only. He would send his spies from there for further reconnaissance, And proceed further (only after their intelligence inputs). (32)
lines: (After so many assurances), the emperor acceded to their request,
But he promised to proceed up to the city of Agra only.
He would send his spies from there for further reconnaissance,
And proceed further (only after their intelligence inputs).

blocks.text: (They must confirm) whether Banda Singh was an angel a human being, And whether he was really (a Man of miracles) or mere fraudulent tricks.
Whether he possessed the power to summon the captive spirits, And whether he really possessed the power to perform miracles. (33)
lines: Whether he possessed the power to summon the captive spirits,
And whether he really possessed the power to perform miracles.

blocks.text: It was said that that neither did Banda Singh leave any footprints, Nor did he bat his eyelids while looking. If it was confirmed that his body cast a shadow on earth, Then alone he (the emperor) would proceed further to confront him. (34)
lines: It was said that that neither did Banda Singh leave any footprints,
Nor did he bat his eyelids while looking.
If it was confirmed that his body cast a shadow on earth,
Then alone he (the emperor) would proceed further to confront him.

blocks.text: Dohra:

(The Muslim clergymen) held out such threats (to Bahadur Shah), And passed several sarcastic strictures against him, The Muslim Pirs and Hajees joined together (in a conspiracy), And swore to (incite the emperor) by placing their hands on the holy Koran. (35)
lines: (The Muslim clergymen) held out such threats (to Bahadur Shah),
And passed several sarcastic strictures against him,
The Muslim Pirs and Hajees joined together (in a conspiracy),
And swore to (incite the emperor) by placing their hands on the holy Koran.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

The designated spies who proceeded to gather intelligence in disguise, Were selected out of the Hindu officials of the emperor's court. Fearing for their lives, they arrived at (Banda Singh's) location, And looked at him and (his movements) very carefully. (36)
lines: The designated spies who proceeded to gather intelligence in disguise,
Were selected out of the Hindu officials of the emperor's court.
Fearing for their lives, they arrived at (Banda Singh's) location,
And looked at him and (his movements) very carefully.

blocks.text: They noticed that Banda Singh left his footprints as he walked, As well as they noticed that his body cast its shadow on earth. They also noticed that he batted his eyelids while expressing anger, And observed him to be a human being rather than being an angel. (37)
lines: They noticed that Banda Singh left his footprints as he walked,
As well as they noticed that his body cast its shadow on earth.
They also noticed that he batted his eyelids while expressing anger,
And observed him to be a human being rather than being an angel.

blocks.text: They (themselves) observed many miracles (performed by Banda Singh), As well as heard about his powers from their confidential resources. So whatever information was conveyed by these intelligence persons, Bahadur Shah accepted their reported information as authentic. (38)
lines: They (themselves) observed many miracles (performed by Banda Singh),
As well as heard about his powers from their confidential resources.
So whatever information was conveyed by these intelligence persons,
Bahadur Shah accepted their reported information as authentic.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Once again when the (Muslim) residents of Punjab appealed to the king, Then the emperor made an attempt (to take action). But after taking his forces out (of the city of Agra), He again ordered them back to enter the city. (39)
lines: Once again when the (Muslim) residents of Punjab appealed to the king,
Then the emperor made an attempt (to take action).
But after taking his forces out (of the city of Agra),
He again ordered them back to enter the city.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

When people appealed yet again (after some time), The Emperor, too, had prepared himself (to take action). After putting thousands of persons carrying copies of Koran in the front, He ordered the Haidari Flag6 to be carried along with his troops. (40)
lines: When people appealed yet again (after some time),
The Emperor, too, had prepared himself (to take action).
After putting thousands of persons carrying copies of Koran in the front,
He ordered the Haidari Flag6 to be carried along with his troops.

blocks.text: He asked the Muslim clergymen and medicants to lead his troops, And keep on reciting Islamic Commandments to remove all fears. Even then the Emperor kept worrying about the consequences, As his confidence kept on waning and waxing (about his success). (41)
lines: He asked the Muslim clergymen and medicants to lead his troops,
And keep on reciting Islamic Commandments to remove all fears.
Even then the Emperor kept worrying about the consequences,
As his confidence kept on waning and waxing (about his success).

blocks.text: This made the emperor to revise his decision in his mind, That he could not afford to strain his relations with Banda Singh. He felt that Banda Singh was the follower of the same Guru, Who had blessed the emperor with the power of sovereignty. (42)
lines: This made the emperor to revise his decision in his mind,
That he could not afford to strain his relations with Banda Singh.
He felt that Banda Singh was the follower of the same Guru,
Who had blessed the emperor with the power of sovereignty.

blocks.text: Since Banda Singh had been invested with great power of miracles, Nobody knew what he might cause to do unto him (the emperor). The Divine angel (Gabriel7 ) who conveyed Prophet Mohammad's Will, Might be the same who sent captive spirits to Banda Singh. Since the same angel had been reported to visit Banda Singh, He might get him (the emperor) killed (at any moment). (43)
lines: Since Banda Singh had been invested with great power of miracles,
Nobody knew what he might cause to do unto him (the emperor).
The Divine angel (Gabriel7 ) who conveyed Prophet Mohammad's Will,
Might be the same who sent captive spirits to Banda Singh.
Since the same angel had been reported to visit Banda Singh,
He might get him (the emperor) killed (at any moment).

blocks.text: Dohra:

So being scared of Banda Singh (for his possession of power of miracles), The emperor once again retreated to his safe sanctuary of) Agra. Since he felt extremely alarmed in his heart of hearts, He did not share his apprehensions with anyone. (44)
lines: So being scared of Banda Singh (for his possession of power of miracles),
The emperor once again retreated to his safe sanctuary of) Agra.
Since he felt extremely alarmed in his heart of hearts,
He did not share his apprehensions with anyone.

blocks.text: Then the emperor thought after a lot of introspection, That he should send a written proposal to Banda Singh. Since both of them were the followers of the same Guru, The emperor would like to pay a visit to Banda Singh. (45)
lines: Then the emperor thought after a lot of introspection,
That he should send a written proposal to Banda Singh.
Since both of them were the followers of the same Guru,
The emperor would like to pay a visit to Banda Singh.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

So the emperor sent a Sikh messenger (with a letter of appreciation), That Banda Singh had performed a noble deed by killing Wazir Khan, And that the hill chiefs whom Banda Singh had also chastised, Were also the most wicked enemies of Guru Gobind Singh. (46)
lines: So the emperor sent a Sikh messenger (with a letter of appreciation),
That Banda Singh had performed a noble deed by killing Wazir Khan,
And that the hill chiefs whom Banda Singh had also chastised,
Were also the most wicked enemies of Guru Gobind Singh.

blocks.text: Although the Emperor himself was keen to kill all those hill chiefs, Yet it was better that Guru's own disciple had dealt with them. The emperor reiterated that he was a humble servant of the Guru, Since it was with the Guru's grace that he had become a sovereign. (47)
lines: Although the Emperor himself was keen to kill all those hill chiefs,
Yet it was better that Guru's own disciple had dealt with them.
The emperor reiterated that he was a humble servant of the Guru,
Since it was with the Guru's grace that he had become a sovereign.

blocks.text: Dohra:

The emperor wrote that there were the tombs of his ancestors, Which were located in the city of Lahore. He proposed that in order to pay his obeisance to them, He wished to go on a pilgrimage to their place of burial. (48)
lines: The emperor wrote that there were the tombs of his ancestors,
Which were located in the city of Lahore.
He proposed that in order to pay his obeisance to them,
He wished to go on a pilgrimage to their place of burial.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

He would visit Banda Singh before his pilgrimage if the latter so desired, Otherwise he would pay his obeisance on his return from Lahore. He requested for a right of passage through the Sirhind province, And sought Banda Singh's permission for a passage upto Lahore. (49)
lines: He would visit Banda Singh before his pilgrimage if the latter so desired,
Otherwise he would pay his obeisance on his return from Lahore.
He requested for a right of passage through the Sirhind province,
And sought Banda Singh's permission for a passage upto Lahore.

blocks.text: He further proposed that half of Punjab territory be handed over to him, While Banda Singh kept his custody over the entire hill states.
He would pay a visit to Banda Singh if the latter permitted, Otherwise he would go to Lahore through the outer fringe of Punjab. (50)
lines: He would pay a visit to Banda Singh if the latter permitted,
Otherwise he would go to Lahore through the outer fringe of Punjab.

blocks.text: (Finally), he pleaded for a permission for a passage upto Lahore, Which should run through the territory of the Sirhind province. With these proposals, he sent a Sikh messenger (to Banda Singh), Who conveyed the emperor's message with folded hands. (51)
lines: (Finally), he pleaded for a permission for a passage upto Lahore,
Which should run through the territory of the Sirhind province.
With these proposals, he sent a Sikh messenger (to Banda Singh),
Who conveyed the emperor's message with folded hands.

blocks.text: Banda Singh, being Omniscient and (privy to all human secrets), Understood all the real motives and intentions of the emperor. Banda Singh realised that Bahadur Shah's proposal for a meeting was a pretence, But, in reality, he was really scared of him (Banda Singh). (52)
lines: Banda Singh, being Omniscient and (privy to all human secrets),
Understood all the real motives and intentions of the emperor.
Banda Singh realised that Bahadur Shah's proposal for a meeting was a pretence,
But, in reality, he was really scared of him (Banda Singh).

blocks.text: Dohra:

After meeting the emperor's emissary, Banda Singh made up his mind, That he should grant Bahadur Shah the right of passage. He would (teach him a lesson) and kill him later on, So that he felt repentant over (his pretence of a pilgrimage). (53)
lines: After meeting the emperor's emissary,
Banda Singh made up his mind,
That he should grant Bahadur Shah the right of passage.
He would (teach him a lesson) and kill him later on,
So that he felt repentant over (his pretence of a pilgrimage).

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Banda Singh sent a reply, accepting Bahadur Shah's proposal, But warning him against reneging from his faith. Banda Singh was allowing him a right of passage for his professing to be a Gursikh, But he would withdraw this concession if the emperor turned a renegade. (54)
lines: Banda Singh sent a reply, accepting Bahadur Shah's proposal,
But warning him against reneging from his faith.
Banda Singh was allowing him a right of passage for his professing to be a Gursikh,
But he would withdraw this concession if the emperor turned a renegade.

blocks.text: As the Sikh messenger brought back Banda Singh's reply, The emperor did not feel concerned at Banda Singh's reply, All the Muslims felt delighted after hearing this reply, And felt optimistic about their better existence in the future. (55)
lines: As the Sikh messenger brought back Banda Singh's reply,
The emperor did not feel concerned at Banda Singh's reply,
All the Muslims felt delighted after hearing this reply,
And felt optimistic about their better existence in the future.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Banda Singh kept the foot hills of the mountains under his custody, And vacated his custodial control over the Punjab. He himself climbed up the mountains (after this decision), After establishing three forts in the foot hills of mountains. (56)
lines: Banda Singh kept the foot hills of the mountains under his custody,
And vacated his custodial control over the Punjab.
He himself climbed up the mountains (after this decision),
After establishing three forts in the foot hills of mountains.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

He got a fort constructed near the town of Sadhaura, Which cameto be known by the name of Lohgarh. Another fort was established in the valley near the Doaba region, So that it might stand like a pillar against the Jaiswal and Kahloor Hill chiefs. (57)
lines: He got a fort constructed near the town of Sadhaura,
Which cameto be known by the name of Lohgarh.
Another fort was established in the valley near the Doaba region,
So that it might stand like a pillar against the Jaiswal and Kahloor Hill chiefs.

blocks.text: The Singhs retreated to the forts inter-connected with each other, Which were located in and around Pathankot near Jammu. Hearing about Banda Singh's movement into the mountains, Bahadur Shah advanced from where his forces were stationed. (58)
lines: The Singhs retreated to the forts inter-connected with each other,
Which were located in and around Pathankot near Jammu.
Hearing about Banda Singh's movement into the mountains,
Bahadur Shah advanced from where his forces were stationed.

blocks.text: Bahadur Shah ordered his forces to march forward, In order to see how Banda Singh reacted to such a move. The emperor wished to see through Banda Singh's motives, And his real intentions (behind such a unilateral withdrawal). (59)
lines: Bahadur Shah ordered his forces to march forward,
In order to see how Banda Singh reacted to such a move.
The emperor wished to see through Banda Singh's motives,
And his real intentions (behind such a unilateral withdrawal).

blocks.text: Dohra:

First of all, Banda Singh (had occupied the territory) up to Panipat, By planting (the Khalsa's saffron) flags on its boundary. These (saffron) flags where no Mughal could dare to come near, Were now ordered to be uprooted by the orders of Banda Singh. (60)
lines: First of all,
Banda Singh (had occupied the territory) up to Panipat,
By planting (the Khalsa's saffron) flags on its boundary.
These (saffron) flags where no Mughal could dare to come near,
Were now ordered to be uprooted by the orders of Banda Singh.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

After the removal of these flags by Banda Singh's orders, The Mughal forces marched forward after crossing Panipat. After putting up a base camp at the town of Karnal, The Mughal forces laid a siege to the entrenched Singhs at Taraori8 (61)
lines: After the removal of these flags by Banda Singh's orders,
The Mughal forces marched forward after crossing Panipat.
After putting up a base camp at the town of Karnal,
The Mughal forces laid a siege to the entrenched Singhs at Taraori8

blocks.text: Dohra:

The Khalsa Singhs had established a police post at Taraori, In the old travellers' inns (after their occupation of this area). When the Mughal forces laid a siege around their positions, The Singhs escaped after cutting through the enemy lines. (62)
lines: The Khalsa Singhs had established a police post at Taraori,
In the old travellers' inns (after their occupation of this area).
When the Mughal forces laid a siege around their positions,
The Singhs escaped after cutting through the enemy lines.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

This Mughal force which had come up to Traori, Arrived at Sirhind to wage a war (against the Khalsa Singhs). Since Banda Singh did not render any support to these Singhs, They deserted Sirhind after waiting in vain for Banda Singh's support. (63)
lines: This Mughal force which had come up to Traori,
Arrived at Sirhind to wage a war (against the Khalsa Singhs).
Since Banda Singh did not render any support to these Singhs,
They deserted Sirhind after waiting in vain for Banda Singh's support.

blocks.text: The Singhs had made revenue collections only for three years, When (Sirhind Province) was taken back from them by the Mughals. As the Singhs entered the fort at Lohgarh in a defiant mood, Mughal forces marched forward after entering Sirhind. (64)
lines: The Singhs had made revenue collections only for three years,
When (Sirhind Province) was taken back from them by the Mughals.
As the Singhs entered the fort at Lohgarh in a defiant mood,
Mughal forces marched forward after entering Sirhind.
